analysis.title: Simon Property Group (SPG) 3Q26 Update: Steady growth continues, with multiple reinvestment levers; Reiterate Buy
key_insights: GS updated its SPG model after 3Q26 earnings, which came in ahead of Visible Alpha consensus and included a full-year guidance increase.

GS 2026 Real Estate FFO estimate is $13.38, above the midpoint of current guidance. GS says guidance could prove conservative if tenant sales momentum continues into the holiday season (comparable tenant sales +4.9% y/y in 3Q26).

GS raised its 12-month price target to $260 from $228, based on a Q5-Q8 target AFFO multiple of 21.2x (from 18.3x). The change reflects revised Q5-Q8 AFFO estimates, rolling AFFO estimates forward a quarter, and the refreshed relationship between REIT growth rates (2025-2028E) and NTM AFFO multiples. SPG currently trades at 19.9x NTM GS AFFO.
FFO estimate shifts are minor and now include 3Q26 actuals, the updated SOFR curve, and updated stock buyback and G&A assumptions.

GS expects NOI upside from permanent occupancy improvement (higher occupancy and a better tenant base) and redevelopment spend. Property acquisitions and buybacks can help offset the FFO impact of refinancing headwinds. GS also expects continued growth in AFFO per share and the dividend.

SPG trades at 16.7x NTM FFO, versus a long-term average (since 2012) of 14.1x. GS argues the average includes periods of weaker sector sentiment and operating conditions that it does not think are relevant today.

SPG trades at a 13% discount to market-cap-weighted REITs (excluding data centers), versus a 2Q13-4Q15 average discount of 1%. GS expects the gap to narrow given SPG's relative FFO growth: Core Real Estate FFO +5.1% in 2026 versus +3.8% for GS REIT coverage.
On AFFO, SPG trades at 18.8x NTM consensus AFFO (average 15.7x), a 16% discount to REITs. That compares with a 2Q13-4Q15 average discount of 3% and a 2Q17-4Q19 average discount of 24%.
On a simple-average basis against 43 REITs, SPG trades at a 21% premium, ahead of its 2Q12-4Q15 average.
GS estimates are 0.7%, 0.6% and 0.5% above Visible Alpha consensus Real Estate FFO for 2026, 2027 and 2028 respectively.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $260 from $228 (12-month, 11.6% upside from $233.01) on a higher target AFFO multiple of 21.2x. GS cites steady growth, a 3Q26 beat and raise, and multiple reinvestment levers.

sector_views.rationale: GS expects SPG's valuation gap versus REITs to narrow on faster FFO growth (+5.1% Core Real Estate FFO in 2026 versus +3.8% for GS REIT coverage).

earnings_insights: 3Q26 results (reported, per GS) came in ahead of Visible Alpha consensus and included a full-year guidance increase.
Comparable tenant sales rose 4.9% y/y in 3Q26.
GS 2026E Real Estate FFO is $13.38 (GS estimate), above the midpoint of guidance. Visible Alpha consensus for 2026E Real Estate FFO is $13.29, as of 11/4/26 and not updated for the 3Q26 release.
GS 2026E NAREIT FFO is $12.78 (previously $13.01), Core FFO is $13.28 to $13.28 new basis ($13.24 previous), and AFFO is $11.43 (previously $11.46). All are GS estimates.
GS 2027E NAREIT FFO is $13.88 (previously $13.91) and AFFO $11.88 (previously $12.02). GS 2028E NAREIT FFO is $14.49 (previously $14.60) and AFFO $12.40 (previously $12.62). All are GS estimates.
GS 4Q26 model assumes the split between fixed and variable lease income stays consistent with 4Q25.

macro_indicators.reading: Updated in GS model; no level given
macro_indicators.interpretation: The updated SOFR curve is one of the inputs to GS's revised FFO estimates. Refinancing remains an interest expense headwind.

risk_factors: Deterioration in mall and outlet retailer operating environments, including tenant sales, leasing volume, new rental rates, shopper traffic and bad debt.
Inability to lower tenant improvement spending.

tension_points.bull_case: SPG trades at a 13% discount to market-cap-weighted REITs, wider than its 1% 2Q13-4Q15 average, and GS expects the gap to narrow given Core Real Estate FFO growth of +5.1% in 2026 versus +3.8% for GS REIT coverage.
tension_points.bear_case: SPG trades at 16.7x NTM FFO versus a 14.1x long-term average, and at a 21% premium to REITs on a simple-average basis. Shares are near an all-time high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deterioration in tenant sales, leasing volume, new rental rates, shopper traffic and bad debt, or higher-than-expected refinancing interest expense.

theme_stances.key_argument: SPG's relative FFO growth should help the valuation gap versus REITs continue to narrow.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect the valuation gap versus REITs can continue to narrow
